paragraphs: Three fostering services list Portsmouth as an area they cover, and all three are shown above: Portsmouth City Council's own service, Foster Portsmouth, and two independent agencies. With the council you care for the city's own children; an agency approves and supports its own carers and takes children councils ask it to place.

When the council opened its 2023 programme of recruitment events, the councillor responsible for children's services said that more than two thirds of the children in its care were aged ten or over. The council asked in particular for people who could foster teenagers, and for carers from a range of backgrounds who reflect the children in care in Portsmouth. A year earlier it had said it especially needed homes that could keep brothers and sisters together.

Foster Portsmouth offers short and long-term fostering, homes for sibling groups, care for disabled children, homes for children seeking safety and asylum, parent and baby placements, respite care and supported lodgings for young people learning to live independently. Carers have a training programme, support around the clock and a mentoring scheme, and the council uses the Mockingbird model, in which a group of fostering households is supported by an experienced hub carer. It also pays for carers' membership of The Fostering Network. The council describes its fees and allowances as competitive but the sources we read did not give figures, so ask for the current rates.
Speak to the council and the agencies above and compare their support. The Hampshire and West Sussex pages list more services in the area.
